The overall review is about male suicide, but the rule requires explicit mention in the text for Population.

Type.evidence_source: The first author, Adrienne Rivlin (AR), conducted face-to-face interviews with participants in private, after obtaining informed consent. The interviews lasted between 30 and 120 minutes. To collect information on the suicidal process we used a semi-structured qualitative interview schedule.

Area.evidence_source: We asked additional follow-up questions in the following four areas: The initial idea of making a suicide attempt: Contributory factors, 'trigger' events, state of mind at the time of the initial idea and purpose of the act. Planning and preparation for the act: Time between the initial idea and act, feelings and emotions during planning and preparation, communication of intent before the act, precautions taken against discovery and final acts including suicide notes. Carrying out the act: Time of incident and reason for timing, whether alone at the time of the act, method used (including severity) and discovery. After the act: Emotions following the act, immediate and long-term consequences, feelings about the act at the time of the interview and reactions to the act from inside and outside prison.
